J1.assembly: Jig the column cage. Thread the lower X and Y rows through their clear corridors, then the upper rows. Keep the two orthogonal row levels distinct. Fit the staggered beam links outside the joint face. Use the central vertical corridor for compaction before closing the forms.
J1.continuity: Interior, non-roof. Centred beams on four faces, no participating slab steel.

J2.assembly: Use prebent links and hooks with temporary positioning during cage assembly. The local reference checks final placement and a vertical compaction corridor. The site insertion sequence and support arrangements require separate verification.

placement.cross_tie_orientation: Both hooks turn into the core. Their planes are staggered.

shape.right_half_installation: Rotate 180 degrees about the transverse horizontal axis.
Rotate 180 degrees about the transverse horizontal axis.

method: Static equilibrium of a declared three-dimensional frame cut with two cores, six beam intervals and four column legs. Each outer cut is represented by its supplied force and moment. Actions are factored witness loads for the bounded frame cut.

Global X east, Y north, Z upward. Vertical beam reactions positive upward on the beam map to positive downwards on the joint. The three-dimensional joint axial balance includes the reactions of both beam planes.

Bending, shear, joint capacity mechanism, confinement and anchorage use the separate independent local sections. The four short column legs use a conservative linear biaxial flexure envelope and shared-hoop shear sum for the concurrent planes.

The shared BX12 stock paths include the west boundary-beam carry-through and straight development in its declared thick support. The boundary support cage, construction-stage handling, insertion and temporary supports require project-specific evidence.
The local joint schedules and the shared beam links use disjoint marks. Local joint views of the eight continuous X bars belong to one shared inventory and carry no duplicate order quantities.
